name: Zacharias and Elisabeth
charge: Both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless
summary: A priest of the course of Abia and a daughter of Aaron, old, childless, and blameless in the whole law. Their prayer was heard at the altar of incense: a son, to be called John, filled with the Holy Ghost from his mother's womb, who would go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elias. Zacharias' unbelief at the news is its own case; the blessing stood.
offense: They were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. He executed the priest's office before God in the order of his course, according to the custom of the priest's office. Elisabeth hid herself five months, saying, Thus hath the Lord dealt with me in the days wherein he looked on me, to take away my reproach among men. On the eighth day they circumcised the child, and against all their kindred named him as the angel had said.
judgment: Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John. And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth. For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord. Her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her. Zacharias was filled with the Holy Ghost and prophesied: and thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest. Christ's own verdict on their son: among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist.

entries.commentary: John hears in the prison the works of Christ and sends two of his disciples to ask, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another? The messiah was spoken of from Genesis forward. They knew he was coming and they knew the description given of him.

Christ answers by pointing to the works: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. He is quoting Isaiah back to them.
Blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.

What went ye out into the wilderness to see? Not a reed shaken with the wind, nor a man in soft clothing, but a prophet, and more than a prophet. John is the messenger written of, sent before the face of the Lord to prepare the way.
Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist, notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

From the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force. The kingdom in view is Israel. The violence is what was done to them, and it is seen plainly in what the Romans did to Jerusalem, taking the kingdom by bloodshed.
All the prophets and the law prophesied until John, and if ye will receive it, this is Elias which was for to come.

That generation is likened to children in the markets who piped and were not danced to. Christ did not move to the beat of their drum. John came neither eating nor drinking and they said he hath a devil; the Son of man came eating and drinking and they called him a gluttonous man. Nothing would have satisfied them.

Woe unto Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum, because the mighty works were done among them and they repented not. Tyre, Sidon and Sodom would have repented at what these cities saw. Men watched works no ordinary man could do and still would not turn.
These things are hid from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. No man knoweth the Father save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. My yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
Praise you the Most High. Praise, O ye servants of the Most High, praise the name of the Most High.
Blessed be the name of the Most High from this time forth and forevermore.
From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same, the name of the Most High is to be praised.
The Most High is high above all nations, and his glory above the heavens. He is letting you know that he is the only God, high above all nations.
Who is like unto the Most High our God, who dwelleth on high?
He humbleth himself to behold the things that are in heaven and in the earth.
He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth the needy out of the dunghill. That is what is happening right now; our people are being lifted up.
That he may set him with princes, even with the princes of his people, which is Israel.

He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise you the Most High. At the bottom he lets you know he can bring our people up from a lower state. He showed the princes and then he showed the women, saying, I can bring the princes up and I can bring the women up.

verses.text: There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea, a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia: and his wife was of the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elisabeth.
And they were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.
And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they both were now well stricken in years.
And it came to pass, that while he executed the priest’s office before God in the order of his course,
According to the custom of the priest’s office, his lot was to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord.
And the whole multitude of the people were praying without at the time of incense.
And there appeared unto him an angel of the Lord standing on the right side of the altar of incense.
And when Zacharias saw him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
And thou shalt have joy and gladness; and many shall rejoice at his birth.
For he shall be great in the sight of the Lord, and shall drink neither wine nor strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Ghost, even from his mother’s womb.
And many of the children of Israel shall he turn to the Lord their God.

And he shall go before him in the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the just; to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.
And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months, saying,
Thus hath the Lord dealt with me in the days wherein he looked on me, to take away my reproach among men.
Now Elisabeth’s full time came that she should be delivered; and she brought forth a son.
And her neighbours and her cousins heard how the Lord had shewed great mercy upon her; and they rejoiced with her.
And it came to pass, that on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child; and they called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
And his mother answered and said, Not so; but he shall be called John.
And they said unto her, There is none of thy kindred that is called by this name.
And they made signs to his father, how he would have him called.
And he asked for a writing table, and wrote, saying, His name is John. And they marvelled all.
And his mouth was opened immediately, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, and praised God.
And fear came on all that dwelt round about them: and all these sayings were noised abroad throughout all the hill country of Judea.
And all they that heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying, What manner of child shall this be! And the hand of the Lord was with him.
And his father Zacharias was filled with the Holy Ghost, and prophesied, saying,
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people,
And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David;
As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began:
That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us;
To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant;
The oath which he sware to our father Abraham,
That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear,
In holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.
And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways;
To give knowledge of salvation unto his people by the remission of their sins,
Through the tender mercy of our God; whereby the dayspring from on high hath visited us,
To give light to them that sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide our feet into the way of peace.
And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his shewing unto Israel.
Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.
He maketh the barren woman to keep house, and to be a joyful mother of children. Praise ye the Lord.
